# Paper Details

**Title:** "Efficiently Identifying Watermarked Segments in Mixed-Source Texts"

**Authors:** Xuandong Zhao, Chenwen Liao, Yu-Xiang Wang, and Lei Li

**Venue:** The 63rd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers), held in Vienna, Austria in July 2025

**DOI:** 10.18653/v1/2025.acl-long.316

The paper addresses detecting watermarked text segments within longer documents by proposing a geometry cover detection framework and an adaptive online learning algorithm. The research evaluates three watermarking techniques and makes code available publicly.

# Paper Details

**Title:** "M-RewardBench: Evaluating Reward Models in Multilingual Settings"

**Authors:** Srishti Gureja, Lester James Validad Miranda, Shayekh Bin Islam, Rishabh Maheshwary, Drishti Sharma, Gusti Triandi Winata, Nathan Lambert, Sebastian Ruder, Sara Hooker, and Marzieh Fadaee

**Venue:** Proceedings of the 63rd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers), held in Vienna, Austria in July 2025

**DOI:** 10.18653/v1/2025.acl-long.3

# Paper Details

**Title:** "AGENTVIGIL: Automatic Black-Box Red-teaming for Indirect Prompt Injection against LLM Agents"

**Authors:** Zhun Wang, Vincent Siu, Zhe Ye, Tianneng Shi, Yuzhou Nie, Xuandong Zhao, Chenguang Wang, Wenbo Guo, and Dawn Song

**Venue:** Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2025 (held in Suzhou, China, November 2025)

**DOI:** 10.18653/v1/2025.findings-emnlp.1258

The paper addresses security vulnerabilities in LLM agents through an automated red-teaming framework using Monte Carlo Tree Search optimization.

# Paper Details

**Title:** "MCIP: Protecting MCP Safety via Model Contextual Integrity Protocol"

**Authors:** Huihao Jing, Haoran Li, Wenbin Hu, Qi Hu, Xu Heli, Tianshu Chu, Peizhao Hu, and Yangqiu Song

**Venue:** Proceedings of the 2025 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP 2025), held in Suzhou, China in November 2025

**DOI:** 10.18653/v1/2025.emnlp-main.62

The paper addresses safety challenges in the Model Context Protocol by proposing an enhanced framework that develops a taxonomy of unsafe behaviors and creates benchmark data to improve language models' abilities in identifying safety risks within MCP interactions.
